comments.text: the house part's entry, where the street part's loader jumps after loading MAIN: JMP $13FE, which sets the house up and falls into the main loop
the first of four hooks the resident disk code calls to show its messages: select text window A (JMP $6817)
hook: wait for a key or the joystick (JMP $6303)
hook: clear the current text window (JMP $6A3E)
hook: print the text at X/Y (high/low) in the current window (JMP $6A83)
a 20-byte scratch line for text built at run time: the drive's status, the clock digits of "IT'S NOW n O'CLOCK", numbers for the panel
a byte the window printer keeps beside the text buffer (read at $6A16)
the end of the scratch line, $FF bytes

the house's table of files for the resident loader, five bytes each: name pointer, load address, disk side (0 for side 1, 1 for side 2). 0 ALTCH.CHA to $A000, 1 SCREEN to $9800, 2 VENDING.SRT to $9000, 3 SCn.DAT (the level's objects) to $8000, 4 Dn (the level's map) to $B000, 5 Dn.CUR (the level's saved state) to $9800, 6 ARTn.ICN to $A000, 7 INIT (the street part) to $1390 on side 1, 8 SAVE.DAT to $9C00, 9 Dn to $A000, 10 DEATH to $9080, 11 COPY to $9800, 12 MSG to $9800, 13 HOUSE to $8000, 14 SONG to $B000. The digits in the level files' names are patched in for the level being entered
JSR $15EA to set the house up, then the main loop

the house's main loop, one pass per round of play: the clock ($1495), Freddy's attacks on the friends ($152B), the player ($234B), the monsters ($494A), shots and powers ($2590), the haunted items ($1439), object animation ($4D0D), the panel ($37BD) and the message timer ($1EF3), until the game-over flag $79C4 is set
game over or a new game: sets $0C4F to 1, pushes $138F as a return address and has the resident loader load file 7, INIT, so that its RTS lands on the street part's entry at $1390

unless the player carries the CRUCIFIX (item $45), a carried FREDDY'S HAT ($43) or FREDDY'S GLOVE ($44) counts down its own timer ($79FA, $79F7) once a pass; at zero the timer is reset to 16, the message reads "<item> IS ATTACKING YOU!" and the player loses 25 health ($440E with X=-25)
" IS ATTACKING YOU!" (CR, $00 ended), printed after the item's name

the clock: subtracts 23 from a fraction byte each pass; on each wrap it counts down the attack timer $79E4, and on level 10 (unless the final fight has started) it counts 120 wraps to an hour, prints "IT'S NOW n O'CLOCK" and calls $5BD2; at 12 o'clock it calls $60EC (turns the level's monsters loose) and sets $73B3
"IT'S NOW " and " O'CLOCK" (CR, $00 ended), around the hour digits in the text buffer

when the attack timer $79E4 runs out it is reset to 240 and Freddy picks a random friend who is neither the player nor rescued: that friend loses a point of soul ($7368, and status 2, dead, at 0), the panel box is redrawn, message 35 and the friend's name are shown with sound 23; if the friend is on the player's level a monster of kind 5 is placed at the friend's spot ($17C7), and a friend who has just died is replaced by object $16 on the map

sets the house up after the load: pointers and the random seed ($164E), the party ($1843), the attack timer, message 1 ("TIME PASSES..."), sound 34, the level's files unless a saved game is being loaded ($572F), the sprites ($16A6), the colours and the panel

copies a block of memory, described by the six bytes after the JSR: source (2 bytes), destination (2 bytes), length (2 bytes); returns past them. Used to keep the screen, colour RAM and character set aside at $9000-$9FFF while a picture or menu covers them, and to bring them back
sets the screen ($CC00) and colour RAM ($D800) pointers the drawing routines use and the text colour, seeds the random generator from the jiffy clock, and empties the keyboard buffer
code nothing calls in the house: switches the video chip to the bank at $C000 through CIA 2, turns the screen's bitmap mode off and the sprites off
the player's sprites: colours (sprite 0 black, the rest white, shared colours 6 and 2), positions 120,125 for sprites 0 and 1, no expansion, sprite 1 multicolour, sprites 0 and 1 on
sets sprite A's X position to Y with bit 8 from X (in $D010)
sets sprite A's Y position to Y
clears the 24 animation counters at $7650, copies every eighth byte of the table at $7578 into $7668, then calls $386C, $384A, $388C and $38AA
clears the eight monster slots, marks each free (kind 6), finds the level's monster list from its number, and places up to six monsters from it at their map spots ($17C7)

puts a monster of kind A at the map cell $79CC,$79CD in slot X, unless the player stands within two cells of it: three of its properties come from the kind tables at $743E, $7482 and $746D, and its picture from $7458; kind 5 takes it from a table indexed by the level instead

starts a game from what the street part handed over: the sound switch ($0C4C), a saved game to load ($0C4D, which goes to $4398), the panel mode ($0C4E) and the character the player chose ($0C4F); the four friends who are not the player are each given one of ten hiding places at random (level, X, Y from $190E, $1918 and $1922), the inventory is emptied ($4D in every slot but the first), and the player starts at the level's entrance
a flag for each of the ten hiding places, cleared as each is handed out so that no two friends share one
the level of each of the ten hiding places
the map column of each hiding place
the map row of each hiding place
draws character X's box in the panel: the name, then "LEVEL n" (the level the friend is held on, or the player's own level), "RESCUED" or "R.I.P.", and the SOUL bar, with the POWR bar for the player
the panel's words: "LEVEL nn", "RESCUED ", "R.I.P.  ", "SOUL", "POWR"
copies a panel word (up to its $00, as screen codes) to the screen at ($61) and colours it white at ($FB)

draws a 3 by 3 character picture of object A (an item, a monster or a map feature) on the screen at column X, row Y, from the 9 character codes and 9 colours at $A800 + A times 18; an animated object ($4E-$65) takes its current frame from $7650 first
copies the 8 bytes of character X of the panel set at $A000 into character Y of the play-area set at $D000, with the I/O switched out for the copy

redraws the 21 rows of the play area from the off-screen copy at $98A7 and $9CA7 (characters and colours, 33 wide), waiting for the raster to be between lines $78 and $88 first so the redraw does not tear; while $79D5 is set, each cell is first tested by $3D5B and a cell it rejects is blanked
$FB-$FC = the address in the level map at $B000 of the cell at column $79CC, row $79CD (64 cells to a row)

puts up the rest of a full-screen picture whose character set the last inline copy moved: a picture file (.SRT) is 2 KB of characters, 1000 screen codes and 1000 colours, so this copies the 1000 bytes at the copy's source plus $0800 to the screen at $CC00 and the next 1000 to colour RAM at $D800, through two inline copies whose sources it patches

shows the player: picks the frame from the facing ($7349, eight directions) and the walking step ($734A) through the tables at $1D34, $1D3D and $1D46, points sprites 0 and 1 (outline and fill) at it and puts them at the centre of the play area (120,125); while $7A13 or $7A14 is set, sprites 2 and 3 are drawn with the same shape beside the player, offset by the direction tables at $7A09 and $7A0B
walking-step to frame, used on even facings
walking-step to frame, used on odd facings
the first frame of each of the eight facings

steps monster X's animation: its sprite shape is the kind's first shape ($746D) plus its direction ($73D2) plus the frame counter ($73F2) times the kind's frame size ($745F), the direction doubled for Freddy (kind 5); the counter wraps at the kind's frame count ($7466)
loop counter for the multiplication in $1D4E
A = the level map's cell at column $79CC, row $79CD
writes A into the level map's cell at $79CC,$79CD and, when that cell is inside the play area, draws its picture there at once ($1D99)
draws the map cell at $79CC,$79CD into the off-screen view if it lies within the 11 by 7 cells around the player ($7342,$7343)
draws object A's 3 by 3 character picture straight onto the screen at column X, row Y, from its 9 characters and 9 colours at $A800 + A times 18; used for the inventory pictures beside the panel

rebuilds the whole off-screen view: for each of the 9 rows and 11 columns of cells around the player draws the map cell's picture ($1A45); a cell off the edge of the 64 by 64 map is drawn as the level's border object ($748F), and on a level with a border object some animated cells are drawn only when the tables at $74A0 and $7490 allow

once a pass: counts down the message timer and shows "TIME PASSES..." when it runs out, steps the animation tick ($79C9) at a random 16 to 23 pass interval, draws the player ($1C8D), puts the monster sprites near the player on screen ($2000; in the final fight the sprites are double size and Freddy has sprite 4), drops sprites 2 and 3 when Freddy's sprite touches them, flickers the light while $79D5 is set, redraws the play area ($1B34) and the shots and powers ($20D6)

puts monster Y on sprite pair X: the screen position comes from its map cell less the player's (8 pixels to a cell), the shape from $73BA (Freddy takes two sprites, and in the final fight his big shape comes from $C000 through $22BE); a monster that has just been hit ($7412) is drawn in a flash colour for one pass; with the light flickering a monster out of its reach is not shown

draws every shot and power effect in the list at $76A2 (column $76A3, row $76AF, kind $76D3): each is a run of characters built into the play area's character set ($1AE2) and laid along its direction, or for kinds 6 and 7 a 5 by 5 pattern from the masks at $22AF
the eight single-bit masks $80 to $01, then three 5-row patterns (a dot, a small cross, a big cross) for the burst effects

copies Freddy's two-sprite final-fight shape from ($6A) into the buffer at $F6C0, then clears the rows and masks the columns that fall outside the play area, given his cell X,Y relative to the view, and points sprites 4 and 5 at it
masks that blank the left or right columns of the shape at the edges
offsets of rows 0 to 5 (in steps of 12 bytes) in the shape, where clearing starts

the player's part of a pass: reads the controls ($4045); on reaching a new map cell runs the cell's trigger ($5BD2) and the square's object handler ($5127); then by the action chosen ($392D): fire button with the stick still uses the equipped item ($2F4C, $3309), a direction walks (sliding along walls, $27DD) or, on a ladder, climbs
counts the four straight directions down from 3 while the walk direction is worked out (written into this LDX)
the stick direction as a single bit, from the table at $2557, written into this AND so each straight direction's mask at $255F can be tested against it
counts down the three neighbouring directions tried when a straight move is blocked (written into this LDX)
the neighbouring direction being tried, from the table at $2577 (written into this LDA)
with no free direction calls $2A19 with A=0; otherwise the free set gives the new facing ($2567) for $7349 and $79D0
the straight directions the player may move in this pass, one bit each (1, 4, 2 and 8 from $2563), built up in this LDX; the table at $2567 turns the set back into one of the eight facings

actions 8 to 14 pick inventory slot 0 to 6 as the item in hand ($7344): an empty slot ($4D) or the slot already in hand does nothing; otherwise the panel is cleared ($2E79), "SELECTED" printed after the item's name (message item code minus $30, or message $27 for slot 0) and sound effect 12 played

actions 15 to 21 drop the item in inventory slot 0 to 6: the slot stands in for the item in hand while $2C89 drops it, then the play area and panel are redrawn ($3309, $2EAD); actions 26 and 27 step the hand to the previous or next item ($2D9A, $2DEB), 23 drops the item in hand, 28 toggles the sound ($674F) and 29 opens the save menu ($5A87)
every action ends here: the action number (written into this LDA) is kept in $79D2, and an action that was not a direction calls $2A19 with A=0
the action $392D chose this pass, written into this LDA at $23AE
one bit for each of the eight stick directions, $80 for direction 0 down to $01 for direction 7
for each straight direction (0, 2, 4, 6) the three stick directions, as bits from $2557, that contain it
the bit each straight direction sets in the free set at $2474
facing for each set of free straight directions (index 0 to 15)
the neighbouring direction to try for each of three tries and four straight directions
added to the straight direction to find the cell checked before a slide (1, 7, 0: the two diagonals and the direction itself)
"SELECTED " and a zero, printed after an item's name when it is put in hand

the monsters' part of a pass, skipped while the counter $79D4 counts down: each of the 8 slots takes 23 from its fraction byte ($73FA); on a borrow it adds the kind's speed ($743E) back until it carries, and the monster acts (kind 6 never moves): measures its distance to the player ($3EEB), picks a direction ($2850, $28AF) and steps ($266D); when it would reach the player it attacks ($44B1); otherwise, within 10 of the player, with a clear line ($2737) and its shot timer ($740A, reloaded from $7482) run out, it fires the kind's shot ($7489) through $5048
the monster slot being moved, 0 to 7 (written into this LDX)
the monster's distance from the player from $3EEB, written into this LDA; at 10 or more it does not shoot

moves monster Y one cell in direction X ($7A01 and $79FF give the column and row steps), keeps the direction in $7402 and its drawn facing in $73D2 (always 0 for kinds 0 and 2, else from $29BE), then steps its animation ($1D4E)

can monster X step in direction Y? Carry set means it can. A monster with flag bit 2 ($73EA) never moves (A=1, carry clear). A target within 2 steps (a step is a third of a cell) of the player in both directions gives A=0, an attack. Otherwise the place is tested with $40AD, in the final fight ($7A15) at the four corners of Freddy's big shape, and carry is set only when every test finds it free
2, or 5 in the final fight, added before the column test (written into this ADC)
5, or 8 in the final fight: how many columns count as reaching the player (written into this CMP)
as $26EE, for the row
as $26F0, for the row
the target column, written into this LDX
the target row, written into this LDY
the monster slot being tested (written into this LDA, passed to $40AD)
how many cells to test: 1, or 4 for Freddy's big shape
column offsets of the four corners tested for Freddy's big shape
row offsets of the same corners

may monster X shoot? Only a kind with flag bit 0 ($73EA) can. Its column and row are divided by 3 ($637C) to give its cell, which is stepped up to four cells along its direction; the walk stops with A=0 at a cell whose type ($7A40) has a clear high nibble, and gives A=1 when it comes within one cell of the player's cell $79CA,$79CB, set by $3DA2
the monster's direction, written into this LDX
counts down the four steps of the line of fire
tests the cell beside the player in direction X with $40AD; carry is set when that test set $7A31

before the player walks in direction X, looks two steps ahead ($3E26): a cell of type $19, or on a level of type 9 ($776A) type $0F, runs its trigger ($5BD2) once until $79FC is cleared; carry set stops the walk
the direction, written into this LDX
set to 1 when the trigger asks the walk to stop (written into this LDA, then BNE)
A = 1 when cell type A has a set high nibble in $7A40 (a cell things can stand in), or is type $0F on a level of type 9 ($776A), else 0; X is kept
X saved over the test, written into this LDX
the direction, of eight, from the cell X,Y to the player's cell $79CA,$79CB, into $28AE: the signs of the two distances and whether one is more than twice the other pick it from the table at $289C
the monster's column, written into this SBC
the monster's row, written into this SBC
the four test results gathered bit by bit (written into this LDX): sign of the column distance, sign of the row distance, row more than twice column, column more than twice row
direction for each of the sixteen results gathered in $2894
the column distance, made positive
the row distance, made positive
the direction to the player that $2850 found

turns a monster's direction A one step towards the direction to the player ($28AE), then tries it and the others in turn, swinging out to alternate sides (which side first follows the animation tick $79C9), with $26A0: carry set and A the direction when the step would reach the player, carry clear and A the direction of a free step; when all eight are blocked A is the direction to the player
the direction being tried (written into this LDY)
the monster slot (written into this LDX)
counts the directions tried, 1 to 8 (written into this LDA)

moves the player one place in direction X (0 up, 2 right, 4 down, 6 left), unless the counter $79D3 holds the player still: changes $7342 or $7343 and the scroll counter $79CE or $79CF; when a counter reaches 3 or -3 the off-screen view is shifted a whole cell (3 characters, $2A19, $2AEF, $2BD7, $2C31) and the new column or row of cells is drawn ($29C6, $2A9C, $2B71), and the counter goes back to 0
the drawn facing (0 to 3) for each of the eight directions, for monsters that turn
draws the column of nine cells five to the left of the player's cell into the left edge of the off-screen view; cells beyond the map's width ($79DE) or height ($79DC) are drawn as object 0
the row in the view being drawn (written into this LDY)
counts the nine cells down

moves every row of the off-screen view (27 rows of 33 characters at $9800, with its colours at $9C00) left by A characters, through four self-written addresses; returns A, so A=0 changes nothing and gives zero
the source address in the character buffer, written into this LDA
the destination address in the character buffer
the source address in the colour buffer
the destination address in the colour buffer
the row being moved, 0 to 26 (written into this LDY)
the number of characters to move by, written into this LDA and returned
as $29C6, for the column five to the right of the player, drawn at the view's column 10
the row in the view being drawn
counts the nine cells down
as $2A19, moving every row right by A characters; returns A
draws the row of eleven cells four rows below (A not 0) or above (A=0) the player's cell into the off-screen view; cells beyond the map are object 0
the column in the view being drawn (written into this LDX)
the row in the view, 8 for the bottom or 0 for the top (written into this LDY)
counts the eleven cells down
with A not 0, moves the off-screen view up by a whole cell (three rows of 33 characters, $63 bytes) and its colours; returns A
the amount, written into this LDA and returned
with A not 0, moves the off-screen view down by a whole cell, working from the bottom; returns A
the amount, written into this LDA and returned

drops the item in hand on the player's cell: only on an empty floor cell (type $16), else "YOU CAN'T PLACE AN ITEM HERE." (message 31); the item's code is written into the map ($1D8D), sound effect 29 plays and the slot is emptied ($4D); dropping the LANTERN ($42) clears the light flag $79D7
the lowest inventory slot holding item A, or $FF when none does (the item is written into the CPY at $2CDB); X and Y are kept and the flags follow A
the item looked for, written into this CPY
X saved over the search
Y saved over the search

picks up object A from the cell the player stands on: BULLETS ($3E) add 10 to the bullet count ($734C), BATTERIES ($3F) add 20 to the battery count ($734E) and COINS ($33) a random 2 to 7 to the coins ($7350), each held at 999; any other item goes into the first empty slot, or with none "YOU CAN'T CARRY ANY MORE ITEMS." (message 30); picking up the LANTERN ($42) sets the light flag $79D7. The item's name and " TAKEN" are printed, the cell becomes floor ($16) and sound effect 28 plays
the item, written into this LDA and stored in the slot
the top of each count, 999 three times
" TAKEN" and a return
action 26: moves the hand to the previous slot holding an item (wrapping from slot 0 to slot 6), marks it in the panel ($2E79) and prints its name and "SELECTED"
the slot the search started from
"SELECTED " and a zero
action 27: as $2D9A, moving to the next slot holding an item
the slot the search started from, written into this CPX
screen address of each inventory slot's marker column in the panel, two bytes a slot
colour memory address of the same places
writes one character of a slot's marker: with A=$5A the marker character in colour 15; otherwise the blank $3B (or $3E beside a picture character of $3A or more, while $7A18 is clear) in colour 10
marks inventory slot $7344 in the panel with A=$5A, or clears the mark with $3B, on the slot's three rows
the character, written into this LDA
redraws the panel's seven inventory pictures ($1DD9 at column 37, rows 0, 3 and so on), marks the slot in hand, and prints the bullet, battery and coin counts ($2EF0)
the slot being drawn, written into this LDX
the screen row of each slot's picture
prints count Y (0 bullets, 2 batteries, 4 coins), held at 999, as up to three digits ($69B1) at its place in the panel
the count's number, 0 to 2 (written into this LDY)
where each count is printed, as offsets from $CF70
copies the digits from the text buffer to the screen at offset X from $CF70 in white, skipping spaces, then pads with spaces to three characters
characters printed so far (written into this LDA)

fire with the stick still: uses the item in hand. With nothing in hand prints "EQUIP SOMETHING, FIRST". An item whose type ($7A40) has bit 6 set is a weapon, sent through the table at $2FD0 by the rest of its type; the MAP, LANTERN, COFFEE, HYPNOCIL and KEY have handlers of their own (table $2F87); anything else gets "WHAT ARE YOU GOING TO DO WITH THAT?"
the handler's address, written into this JMP

handlers for items $41 to $4B: MAP $3034, LANTERN $2FE8, HAT, GLOVE, CRUCIFIX and JUMP ROPE $2FB5, COFFEE $2FE9, HYPNOCIL $3008, HOLY WATER and MAGNET $2FB5 (the HOLY WATER never gets here: it is a weapon, type 7), KEY $3275
"EQUIP SOMETHING, FIRST"
prints "WHAT ARE YOU GOING TO DO WITH THAT?" (message 41)
jumps to the handler for weapon type A from the table at $2FD0, with the type left in A
the type, written into this LDA
the handler's address, written into this JMP

handlers by weapon type, the item's $7A40 entry less bit 6: DAGGER 0, BASEBALL BAT 1 and AXE 2 strike ($4B7B), PICK 3 ($49D3), CHAIN SAW 4 ($4A41), the special power 5 ($4C0B), GRENADE 6 and HOLY WATER 7 are thrown ($4C9B), TASER 8, PISTOL 9, ICE GUN 10 and SHOTGUN 11 fire ($4AAB)
the LANTERN does nothing when used: it works by being carried
COFFEE: at full health ($7345 equal to $7347) prints "NO NEED...YOU'RE FULLY HEALED"; otherwise it is used up and heals 20 plus a random amount ($440E)
HYPNOCIL: unless both health ($7345) and the second meter ($7346) are full, it is used up, heals 40 ($440E) and fills the second meter by 15 ($4055)

the MAP: saves the play area, its character set and part of the house's data ($1290, $9000 to $9CFF) out of the way with $1633, draws the whole 64 by 64 level as a picture of 2 by 2 dots ($3163), shows the player as a blinking sprite dot, waits for the fire button, then puts everything back and redraws the view
$1633's arguments: $9000 to $0F00, $0100 bytes
the character set at $C000 to $9000, $0800 bytes
the screen at $CC00 to $9800, $03E8 bytes
the colours at $D800 to $9C00, $03E8 bytes
the dot sprite's colour, flipped each wait (written into this LDA)
$9000 back to $C000, $0800 bytes
$9800 back to $CC00
$9C00 back to $D800
$0F00 back to $9000
$033C back to $1290
the colour, 0 to 3, each map cell type is drawn in on the map, four to a byte

clears the screen ($3256) and the character set at $C000, lays characters 0 to 255 out as a block of 16 by 16 in the middle of the screen, then reads every cell of the level map at $B000 and plots it ($3219) in the colour $3149 gives its type
the first character of the row being laid out
the address of the map cell being read, written into this LDA
the map column being drawn, 0 to 63
the map row being drawn, 0 to 63
sets the double-wide dot for map column X, row Y to colour A, two pixel rows high, in the character set at $C000
the colour, written into this LDA
clears the screen at $CC00 and its colours to 0

the KEY: the player must face up or left, else "YOU NEED A DOOR TO USE THAT!"; a door ahead (cell types $04 and $24 across, $0A and $27 up and down) becomes open floor in both its cells, $35AA is called, the view is redrawn, sound effect 7 plays and the key is used up; with no door ahead sound effect 35 plays and the message is shown

when the hand holds nothing or the MAGNET ($4A), puts the best weapon carried in hand, searching the table at $3368 from the TASER down to the DAGGER and skipping a gun with no bullets or batteries left; prints its name and " AUTO-SELECTED"
the slot found (written into this LDX)
the weapons from worst to best: DAGGER, PICK, BASEBALL BAT, AXE, CHAIN SAW, PISTOL, SHOTGUN, ICE GUN, TASER
which count each needs: 0 none, 1 bullets, 2 batteries
" AUTO-SELECTED", a return and a zero

the pieces $35AA adds to the map beyond a door, 16 bytes each: a 4 by 4 grid of test codes, one to a half byte, that the map must match, then a 4 by 4 grid of codes to write; 11 pieces for doors opened facing up from here, 9 facing right from $343A, 6 facing down from $34CA and 8 facing left from $352A

after a door is opened, tunnelled or blown at the map cell X,Y in direction A, tries to add a 4 by 4 piece of map beyond it: the place must lie inside the map and the cell there must be closed (an open cell gives A=2, carry set); on a level that grows ($79FD, from the level table at $77AD) each piece listed for the direction ($338A) is tested against the map ($3667) and the first that fits is written in ($36B9), carry clear. A level that does not grow gives A=0, and no piece fitting A=1, both with carry set
the direction halved, 0 to 3 (written into this LDX)
added to the map pointer to reach the piece's corner, for each direction
offset of the cell that must not be solid, for each direction
how many pieces each direction has: 11, 8, 9 and 6
where each direction's pieces start
the lowest column a piece may start at, for each direction
one past the highest column
the lowest row
one past the highest row

tests a piece's first grid against the 4 by 4 cells at ($FB),Y: code 14 matches anything, 7 needs an open cell or type $0D, any other code n needs a cell below $29 whose property word ($7AA8) has bit n set; A=1 when every cell matches, else 0

writes a piece's second grid into the map: code 15 leaves the cell, 8 and 9 turn a cell with property bit 5 or 6 into cell 1 or $0D, 5 and 6 write a random wall piece ($375E, $374F), any other code n the cell from the table at $3720
the map cell written for codes 0 to 7
the next half byte of the piece at ($6C): the high half on even counts, the low half on odd ones, stepping on after the low half
steps Y to the next cell of the 4 by 4 grid: along the row, or to the start of the next map row (64 cells on) after every fourth cell
a random one of the cells $08, $09, $23 and $24
a random one of the cells $02, $03, $21 and $22

runs the effect of the cell the player stands on ($7A3B): a cell type with bit 7 set belongs to effect group (type and $7F); when the group is on for the level ($7490), on every other count of its timer ($7498) and when the cell's animation frame ($7650) has its bit set in the cell's mask ($7638), jumps to the group's handler from the table at $7680
the cell's frame mask, written into this AND
the group, written into this LDA so that the handler gets it in A
